reviews.lens: product and UX fit (ElevenLabs Reader replacement)
strengths: Goal order is right: the listening loop (import, play, screen-off, resume) comes first and expressiveness second, which matches how ElevenLabs Reader is actually used.
A CPU Kokoro default tier that spends no ZeroGPU quota, plus a MeloTTS fallback on Workers AI, means the app can always produce audio. That reliability is the base a premium feel needs.
Cache keys are content-addressed (engine, voice, settings, text), so re-listening, resuming and switching between devices cost nothing and start instantly once rendered.
Segments of 1 to 4 sentences, each over 5 s, are aligned to sentence boundaries. That supports sentence highlighting and tap-to-seek, and keeps the Android media notification alive.
Clone references are stored with their transcripts and the director uses structured spans, so the source text can never be rewritten. Both choices protect quality.
The audio pipeline keeps dynamics: one static gain to -18 LUFS with no compression, which keeps the expressive range intact.

issues.problem: Screen-off playback is goal #1, but the plan only says 'one audio element' that requests the next window. In practice that means changing src on 'ended' for every 5-30 s segment. With the screen off on One UI, this risks audible gaps, Chrome refusing play() after a src change in the background, a notification that flickers or resets, and a lock-screen scrubber that covers one segment rather than the document. The native-shell fallback is deferred to phase 3, and there is no device test in tonight's acceptance checks.
issues.fix: Play through MediaSource Extensions with one SourceBuffer of type audio/webm;codecs=opus. Chrome's MSE does not accept Ogg, so have the Space emit WebM/Opus instead of Ogg. Append each segment with timestampOffset to build one continuous timeline per chapter. Call navigator.mediaSession.setPositionState with chapter duration and position, and set MediaMetadata with title, chapter and cover artwork. Map seekbackward/seekforward to ±15 s and previoustrack/nexttrack to the previous or next paragraph, which also covers Bluetooth headset buttons. Keep at least 3 minutes buffered ahead so a network stall in the background never empties the buffer. Add an acceptance check for tonight: 20 minutes on the A12 with the screen off and the app installed, zero gaps over 300 ms, and notification controls working. If it fails, promote the native shell from phase 3.

issues.problem: There is no first-run flow that deals with Samsung battery management, which is the most likely reason the app 'stops working' on an A12 with nothing on screen to explain it.
issues.fix: Build a one-time setup screen after login with three steps. First, an install prompt (capture beforeinstallprompt). Second, a 2-minute screen-off test clip: compare audio.currentTime against wall clock on resume to detect whether playback was killed. Third, if it was killed, show the exact steps: Settings > Apps > Chrome (and the installed app) > Battery > Unrestricted, and remove it from Sleeping apps and Deep sleeping apps. Save the result and offer to rerun it from Settings.

issues.problem: Goal 2 (expressive reading inferred from the text) is absent from the default path. Kokoro has no emotion control, and the director only runs for the GPU tier, which has 5 GPU-min/day and perhaps 3 runs. So about 95% of listening is flat narration, while the brief and the user expect expressiveness by default.
issues.fix: Run the director (Workers AI Gemma, about 50 neurons per call, about 200 calls/day within the 10k neurons) on Standard-tier text too, and map its output onto controls Kokoro does have. Speaker attribution for quoted dialogue assigns one of the curated Kokoro voices per character, with the narrator voice for the rest. Emotion becomes per-segment speed changes of ±8% and pause lengths (inserted silence of 150-700 ms at paragraph, scene-break and dialogue boundaries). Put these fields in the cache key. Label the tiers honestly in the UI: 'Standard (multi-voice)' versus 'Expressive (your voice / Ming)'.

issues.problem: Playback speed control is missing entirely. ElevenReader offers 0.25x to 4x, and it is the most-used reader control. Rendering speed on the engine side would also split the cache by speed.
issues.fix: Do speed on the client: audio.playbackRate with preservesPitch=true (the default). Keep speed out of the cache key. Add a speed sheet from 0.5x to 3x in 0.05 steps with 1.0/1.25/1.5/2.0 chips, saved per user with an optional per-document override. Show 'time left' as remaining characters ÷ measured characters-per-second ÷ speed. Play voice previews at the current speed.

issues.problem: There is no sleep timer, skip control, bookmark or tap-to-play-from-here. These are standard ElevenReader features, and their absence makes the app feel like a prototype.
issues.fix: Add a sleep timer with 15/30/45/60 minutes and 'end of chapter'. Check the deadline in the audio 'timeupdate' handler rather than setTimeout so background throttling cannot break it, and fade the volume to 0 over the last 10 s before pausing. Add ±15 s buttons and paragraph next/previous in the full player. Tapping any sentence in the text view seeks to that segment. Add long-press on a sentence to bookmark it with an optional note, stored in D1.

issues.problem: D1 lists 'progress' but no semantics. Audio time differs per voice and per tier, so a position saved as seconds breaks when the user switches voice, when the fallback engine was used, or when the director changes pauses.
issues.fix: Store progress as (doc_id, char_offset into the normalised text, updated_at). Write it to IndexedDB every 5 s and on pause; sync it to the Worker on pause, on visibilitychange=hidden (navigator.sendBeacon) and every 30 s. On resume, find the segment containing char_offset and start from the start of that sentence, minus one sentence so the listener gets context back. Show 'Continue <title> at 42%' as the first card on the home screen.

issues.problem: Offline listening is deferred to phase 2, and the audio path is server-streamed (GET /api/audio with Range). D2 assumes a local audio cache that this design never builds. On mobile data or the Underground, playback stops.
issues.fix: Ship it tonight as a rolling cache: every segment played or prefetched is stored as a Blob in the Cache API or IndexedDB, keyed by cache key, and fed into the MSE buffer from there. Also cache the app shell and library in the service worker so the app opens offline. Add a 'Download' action per document: render the whole document on the Standard tier through the Queue in batches of 20 segments and store them locally, with progress shown on the library card and the size in MB. Give interactive render requests priority over download batches in the Space queue (separate Gradio endpoints, with downloads at concurrency_limit=1).

issues.problem: Time to first audio is unspecified and likely slow. The Worker waits for the whole window's SSE run before returning. Kokoro's speed on a 2 vCPU Space is unmeasured (about 3.5 s to first output on an older i7), and ffmpeg encode plus the R2 upload sit in the critical path. Two to five seconds of silence after pressing play feels broken next to ElevenReader. At 2-3x playback speed, a CPU renderer at about 2-4x realtime will also stall.
issues.fix: Pre-render the first 3 minutes as soon as a document is imported, before play is pressed, so play is a cache hit. On a cold play, request count=1 first and then the larger window. Have the Worker return each segment as its 'generating' SSE event arrives rather than at 'complete'. Measure Kokoro's realtime factor on the Space tonight and set the prefetch depth to the max speed (3x) divided by that RTF. If the RTF is below 4x, show a 'buffering ahead' indicator instead of stalling silently, and suggest the Download action.

issues.problem: Quota exhaustion has no UX. The cloned voice, voice design and previews all draw on about 5 GPU-min and possibly 3 runs a day, shared with streams-engine. The plan's 'shows progress and plays when ready' leaves the user stuck when the job fails with a quota or runs-limit error.
issues.fix: Keep a local quota ledger in D1: GPU seconds requested per call, runs used, and reset time (24 h after first use), corrected from the 'exceeded your GPU quota' and 'runs limit' error strings. Show it in the voice picker: 'Your voice: about 3 min left today, resets 21:14'. Give each cloned or designed voice a stand-in Kokoro voice, chosen once by gender and pitch, during cloning. When quota runs out mid-document, keep playing in the stand-in voice with a one-line notice and queue the remaining expressive segments for after reset. Never let playback stop. Make the Kaggle overnight bulk render an explicit 'Render this book in my voice tonight' button with an ETA.

issues.problem: The clone flow ('record 20-60 s in the app') is underspecified for a phone mic. Chrome's default getUserMedia applies echo cancellation, noise suppression and AGC, which degrade a clone reference. There are no quality checks, the preview spends one of perhaps 3 daily GPU runs, and Whisper is redundant when the user reads a known script.
issues.fix: Record with {echoCancellation:false, noiseSuppression:false, autoGainControl:false, channelCount:1}, using MediaRecorder at 128 kbps Opus or WAV through an AudioWorklet. Show a live level meter. Reject the take if it clips (peak > -1 dBFS) or if the noise floor measured in a 2 s silent lead-in is above -50 dBFS, and show why. Record the script sentence by sentence with per-line re-record. Use the script text as the transcript, and run Whisper only for uploaded files, which the flow should also accept. Check Ming's maximum reference length. If it is shorter than the recording, choose the cleanest 10-20 s window automatically. Render one 10 s preview in a single GPU call and state on screen that it uses 1 of today's runs.

issues.problem: Import misses the main way ElevenReader gets content on Android: sharing a link or file from another app. URL import also runs readability parsing (dom_smoothie) in the Worker, where the 10 ms CPU limit will fail on large pages.
issues.fix: Add a manifest share_target. Use method GET with params title, text and url for links. Use method POST, enctype multipart/form-data and accept ['.epub', '.pdf', '.txt', '.md', '.html'] for files, handled in the service worker. Shared items land in the library with a toast and start pre-rendering. Change the Worker so it only fetches raw HTML (network time is not billed) and returns it; run dom_smoothie extraction in the browser wasm alongside segmentation. Switch the session cookie from SameSite=Strict to Lax so a share-launched navigation still carries the session.

issues.problem: Tonight's scope bundles cloning, voice design, director, queue, cron, fallback and four importers, with no acceptance check on the actual phone. The listening loop may ship broken while secondary features take the time.
issues.fix: Define milestone A, which must pass on the A12 before starting anything else: paste/URL/EPUB/share import, Kokoro play, gapless MSE, 20 minutes screen-off, resume, speed, sleep timer, rolling offline cache. Milestone B follows: clone, Ming, director, quota UX. Write both as checklists in the plan note and mark each item verified on the device.

issues.problem: The voice catalogue exposes all Kokoro voices, of very uneven quality, and Ming voices on GPU. Browsing with live previews would spend quota and feel unfinished.
issues.fix: Curate 6-8 English Kokoro voices from the top grades in Kokoro's VOICES.md, each with a human name, accent and tone tags and a description. Pre-render a 10 s preview for every catalogue voice, Ming ones included (one GPU batch at deploy time through xtask), and store them in R2. Play previews at the listening speed. Allow a default voice plus a per-document override.

issues.problem: Text normalisation doesn't cover what makes TTS sound amateur: citation markers like [12], footnote numbers, URLs, PDF running headers and footers, page numbers, line-end hyphenation, tables and code blocks. There is also no pronunciation dictionary, which ElevenReader has.
issues.fix: In nolabs-text, drop bracketed numeric citations and superscript footnote refs, and replace URLs with their domain. For PDFs, remove lines that repeat across 3 or more pages at the same position, remove bare page numbers, and join hyphenated line ends. Skip code blocks and tables with a short spoken 'code block skipped'. Add a user pronunciation dictionary (word to respelling), applied before the cache key. Show a 'review text' step after a PDF or EPUB import with the chapter list and a toggle to skip front matter.

issues.problem: The fallback to MeloTTS changes the voice silently when the Space is down. MeloTTS output may also not be WebM/Opus, which breaks a single MSE timeline.
issues.fix: Show a small 'Backup voice' badge on the player while fallback audio plays. Re-request those segments in the intended voice once the Space health check passes, and swap them in at the next segment boundary. Have the Worker queue a transcode job, or play fallback segments through a second audio element, so the main timeline keeps one codec.

issues.problem: The library and player don't specify the visual features that read as premium: covers, progress, mini-player, lock-screen artwork, chapter navigation.
issues.fix: Use EPUB cover images or the article's og:image as covers, with gradient placeholders generated from a title hash. Show a progress bar and 'X min left' on each card. Keep a persistent mini-player above the nav, with a full player for text and highlighting (word-level for Kokoro, sentence-level for Ming). Pass the cover as MediaMetadata artwork at 512 px. Add a chapter list sheet, a dark theme by default and tap targets of at least 48 px for the 6.5-inch screen.

reviews.lens: Feasibility on free tiers and operational reliability
strengths: Making Kokoro on the Space CPU the default narrator is the only Standard tier that fits the budget. Source-verified: CPU endpoints use neither GPU seconds nor runs.
The Space writes Opus straight to R2, so audio bytes never pass through the Worker's 10 ms CPU budget.
A content-addressed cache key (engine, voice, settings, normalised text) in R2 means no segment is ever rendered or paid for twice.
Long GPU jobs run in a Queue consumer (15 min wall time), not inside the phone's HTTP request. One GPU call per batch fits the run-count limit.
MeloTTS on Workers AI costs 18.63 neurons per audio minute. It is a fallback that has no dependency on Hugging Face.
Pinned stack (gradio 6.17.3, Python 3.10, transformers 4.46.3) has a verified resolve and avoids the huggingface-hub conflict.

issues.problem: The cloned voice and emotional fiction cannot be delivered for real listening on ZeroGPU. The Ming Space's own estimate is 40 s + 0.2 s per character, admission multiplies the request by 1.5, and the cap is 3 runs or 300 s a day. The largest admissible first request is about 200 s, which is roughly 800 characters, or about 1 minute of audio per run and about 3 minutes a day. If the requested duration is set below the real time, ZeroGPU kills the task and the run is lost. v1 lists 'your cloned voice, emotional fiction, voice design, previews' as if they were usable daily features.
issues.fix: Spend one GPU run tonight measuring Ming's real-time factor on a 600-character batch. Set duration = measured_rtf x estimated_audio_s x 1.3 + 15 s, with a hard limit of remaining_quota / 1.5. Write the measured daily audio capacity into note 06 and size the tiers from it. Treat the cloned voice tonight as short passages and previews only. Move the Kaggle bulk renderer for whole books in the cloned voice to the top of phase 2.

issues.problem: Testing tonight can use up the whole day's GPU budget. The plan already sets aside 4 calls to measure the runs limit. Smoke tests of render_gpu and design_voice, plus the end-to-end test through the Worker, each burn a run. After about 3 runs, any bug found in the expressive path cannot be retested for 24 h (the reset is rolling, from first use, not at midnight). That makes 'everything working tonight' unreachable for the Expressive tier.
issues.fix: Add a DEVICE environment switch to the Space so render_gpu can run Ming on the CPU (0.5B, one sentence) for contract and smoke tests that use no quota (assumed to work: verify MingTTS(device='cpu') once). Unit-test the Worker's GPU job flow against a fake Space endpoint. Tonight, spend at most 2 real GPU runs: one RTF measurement and one end-to-end job. Run the runs-limit probe (4th call) tomorrow.

issues.problem: GPU jobs are not idempotent. A Queue retry, a cron 'recover stuck jobs' resubmit, or a consumer killed at the 15 min wall (possible while a low-quota free user waits in the ZeroGPU queue) each call render_gpu again and burn another of the 3 daily runs. The original Gradio job may still finish and upload. Errors that should not be retried ('exceeded your ZeroGPU runs limit', 'quota ... Try again in X') get retried as well.
issues.fix: Set the consumer to max_retries=0 for the GPU queue. Before submitting, write the job row with state 'submitted' and the deterministic output keys. The Space writes a completion marker to R2 at jobs/{job_id}.json after uploading. The consumer and cron check that marker before they ever resubmit. Parse the error text: 'runs limit' and 'quota' set state 'deferred' with retry_at = the parsed wait time, and nothing else is retried automatically.

issues.problem: The Standard press-play path holds the phone's HTTP request open while the Space renders, and the Worker writes the D1 manifest only after the SSE 'complete' event. If Android throttles or drops the request with the screen off, or the user seeks, the Worker is cut off 30 s later (waitUntil limit). The audio lands in R2 with no manifest, and the next request re-renders it. Waiting for the whole window also delays first audio until every segment in the window is done. That is unmeasured: at 2x realtime, 4 segments of 30 s take about 60 s.
issues.fix: Make R2 the source of truth. The Space uploads each segment with x-amz-meta (duration, timings key) and also writes a small timings JSON. On a D1 miss, the Worker does one R2 head on the cache key before rendering. Make render_cpu a Gradio generator that yields per segment. The Worker streams NDJSON lines to the app as each segment completes (Response::from_stream). The first request in a session is 1 short segment (≤150 chars), then windows of 4.

issues.problem: Kokoro speed on the ZeroGPU Space CPU is unmeasured, and the 2 vCPU figure is assumed. Gradio's default concurrency of 1 serialises prefetch and seek. Ming's CPU-side work and the ffmpeg/pyloudnorm encode share the same cores. Below about 1.5x realtime, playback stalls. v1 renders only on demand, so any Space outage or slowdown is heard right away.
issues.fix: Measure Kokoro RTF first tonight, using 1,000 characters on the deployed Space. Also render ahead in the background: on import, enqueue the whole document in Queue messages of 20 segments each (a 3,000-segment book is about 450 queue ops, well under 10k/day), so listening mostly comes from R2. If RTF is below 1.5x, add the GitHub Actions Kokoro renderer (public repo, unlimited standard runner minutes, writes to R2) as a second Standard source.

issues.problem: Free limits are per account, and the Cloudflare account already runs 15 Workers, the R2 bucket pstream-data and a cron. The 100k requests/day, 10 GB-month of R2 storage, 10k neurons/day and 10k queue ops/day are all shared with the Streams project. Audio Range requests, job-status polling (every 2 s is 1,800 requests an hour) and the keepalive add to the count. Error 1027 or a full R2 quota would stop the reader and Streams together.
issues.fix: Tonight, read current usage through the Cloudflare GraphQL analytics API (workersInvocationsAdaptive, r2StorageAdaptiveGroups) and the pstream-data size, and record them in notes. Poll jobs with backoff (5 s up to 30 s) or stream progress over one request. Have the service worker cache each audio key so it is fetched once. Add an R2 lifecycle rule on nolabs-media (for example, delete audio/ after 60 days), and keep a daily request counter in D1 that switches off prefetch above 70k.

issues.problem: Fallback detection is not specified. When the Space is sleeping, rebuilding (the disk is wiped on restart, so torch and model files are fetched again, which takes minutes) or in RUNTIME_ERROR, a Gradio call can hang or return a 503 HTML page. Nothing says when the Worker gives up and switches to MeloTTS. It is also unclear whether a request to a sleeping private Space wakes it.
issues.fix: The cron (one trigger every 30 min) reads GET /api/spaces/{repo}/runtime. If the stage is SLEEPING, PAUSED or RUNTIME_ERROR, it calls POST /api/spaces/{repo}/restart and records the stage in D1. Render requests check that row: if the stage is not RUNNING, or no SSE 'process_starts' event arrives within 8 s, the Worker renders the segment with MeloTTS under a separate cache key (engine=melotts) and re-renders it with Kokoro later. Use preload_from_hub for Kokoro, its voices, en_core_web_sm and the Ming weights, so cold start skips the downloads.

issues.problem: Importing a large document through the Worker can exceed 10 ms of CPU. In v1, the app posts title, source and every segment as one body, and the Worker writes a D1 row per segment. A 1 MB EPUB text parsed with serde in wasm, then hashed and turned into thousands of insert bindings, can hit error 1102. Free D1 allows 50 queries per invocation, and (from memory, verify) about 100k rows written per day. With indexes, a few books a day would fill that.
issues.fix: Stream the raw body to R2 without parsing it (R2 put with a FixedLengthStream; the app sends Content-Length). Store the segment list as one R2 JSON object per document, so D1 keeps only documents, progress, voices, jobs and cache manifests. Look up cache hits for a window with a single SELECT ... WHERE key IN (...). Group all D1 writes in one db.batch(), which counts as one query.

issues.problem: Workers AI's 10k neurons/day is a hard stop that the director, Whisper, MeloTTS and any other Streams Worker all draw from. On a heavy director day the MeloTTS fallback dies too, so the claim that 'the app never goes silent' fails exactly when it is needed. The ASR check adopted in note 02 is missing from v1. Run on Workers AI it would cost 46.63 neurons per audio minute from the same pool.
issues.fix: Keep a neuron ledger in D1, using the published per-token and per-minute prices. Cap the director at 6,000 neurons/day and reserve 3,000 for MeloTTS (about 160 min of fallback audio). Run the ASR check in the Space on CPU (faster-whisper base) for GPU outputs only, not on Workers AI.

issues.problem: The clone reference does not match the Ming code path. v1 records 20 to 60 s, but the community Space truncates references to MAX_REF_SECONDS = 20, so the full transcript would no longer match the cut audio. Android MediaRecorder produces webm/opus, which Workers AI Whisper may not accept, and base64-encoding a long WAV in the Worker costs CPU.
issues.fix: The Space converts the recording on the CPU with ffmpeg to 24 kHz mono WAV. It picks the best sentence-aligned 10 to 18 s span, using the guided script's known text as the transcript, so Whisper is needed only to verify. Store {ref_key, transcript} for that span only.

issues.problem: Each voice preview and each voice-design attempt costs a whole GPU run. A user trying three designs spends the day's runs before reading anything.
issues.fix: Ship the static sample clips for Ming's built-in voices and render Kokoro previews on the CPU. Render 3 design variants in one GPU call and keep the chosen one. Show the remaining runs and seconds from the D1 quota ledger in the UI before any GPU action.

issues.problem: Creating the second ZeroGPU Space can be blocked for eligible free accounts (forum reports from July to October 2026). Both the Standard and Expressive tiers live in that one Space, so it is a single point of failure for tonight and afterwards.
issues.fix: Create the Space through POST /api/repos/create with hardware zero-a10g as the very first step tonight. If that fails, the Standard tier runs from the GitHub Actions Kokoro renderer writing to R2 with MeloTTS for live gaps, and Expressive waits for Kaggle. Keep the Space and Worker contract identical so the source of audio is a config value.

issues.problem: Creating R2 S3 credentials is not specified, and the Space needs them. If the upload fails after a GPU render, the run is wasted.
issues.fix: In xtask, call POST /accounts/{id}/tokens with the Global API Key to create an account-owned token. Scope it to Workers R2 Storage Bucket Item Write on com.cloudflare.edge.r2.bucket.{account_id}_default_nolabs-media. The access key id is the token id and the secret is the SHA-256 hex of the token value. Push both with POST /api/spaces/{repo}/secrets. In the Space, use boto3 with region 'auto' and request_checksum_calculation='when_required' (assumed precaution), and call head_bucket at startup and report the result in /health. The Worker refuses GPU jobs while storage is unhealthy. On upload failure, the Space also returns the file as a Gradio output so the consumer can copy it.

issues.problem: The quota is reported through /api/spaces/zero-gpu/quota, which needs a token with the billing-read permission. The stored token is a classic 'write' token, and keeping it in the Worker exposes every repo on the account.
issues.fix: Create a fine-grained HF token scoped to the nolabs-engine repo (read, write for restart) plus billing read, store that one in the Worker, and keep the account-wide write token on the Mac. If the quota endpoint fails, fall back to the D1 ledger (requested and actual seconds and run count per call, 24 h rolling from first use).

issues.problem: Deploying static assets through the raw API needs the assets upload session (manifest, hashes, completion token). That is the fiddliest part of a Node-free deploy and could take up an evening's debugging.
issues.fix: Tonight, embed the trunk dist in the Worker with include_bytes! (about 300 KB, well under the 64 MiB and 1 s startup limits), or use the wrangler 4.156.0 already installed under ~/.local/node as D3's fallback. Build the Rust assets uploader afterwards.

issues.problem: Phase 2 assumes Ming runs on Kaggle's T4 or P100. Neither GPU has native bf16, and Kaggle needs a phone-verified account for GPU and internet access. Throughput there is unknown.
issues.fix: Before building the Kaggle path, run a 1-sentence Ming job on a Kaggle T4 in fp16 and in fp32 and record the RTF and audio quality. Also check the account's phone verification through the Kaggle API.

reviews.lens: Software architecture and code quality (layers, crate split, logic placement, testability, Worker/Space contract, errors, migrations, xtask deploy, CI)
strengths: The three layers are split correctly. The always-on Worker owns state, the Space only runs models, and the phone is a client. Each piece fits the free-tier constraints in note 03.
The Space writes Opus straight to R2 over S3, so audio bytes never pass through the Worker's 10 ms CPU budget.
Content-addressed audio cache keyed by sha256 makes R2 layout migrations trivial and lets audio be served with immutable caching.
The director returns structured spans instead of rewritten text, so validation can be pure and fully unit tested.
Pure crates (core, text) are kept separate from I/O crates (worker, web), and every resource gets a nolabs- prefix so existing Streams resources are not touched.
The xtask smoke test against the live API (login, import, render, fetch, duration check) is the right acceptance gate.
Pinning Gradio 6.17.3 and Python 3.10 and vendoring Ming follows the verified dependency resolve and removes the api.mrfake.name runtime dependency.

issues.problem: In data flow step 4 the Standard tier runs synchronously: the Worker holds the Gradio SSE stream open inside the phone's POST /api/render. The core use case is screen-off playback. When Android backgrounds Chrome or the connection drops, the request ends and waitUntil gives only 30 s, so renders get cut off mid-batch and leave nothing in D1. Kokoro CPU speed is unmeasured, so these requests may also take tens of seconds. There are also two separate job paths (sync for CPU, queued for GPU) to build and test.
issues.fix: Use one job path for both tiers. POST /api/render hashes the segments, claims misses in D1, sends one Queue message per batch (batch_size 1, minimum max_batch_timeout), and returns at once with {key, status} per segment. The Queue consumer (15 min wall time) holds the SSE stream. The client polls GET /api/render/status?keys=... every 1-2 s, or just GETs /api/audio/{key} and retries on 404. Have the Space also write a sidecar audio/{key}.json manifest to R2, so the cron can rebuild D1 rows from R2 if a consumer dies.

issues.problem: Several Worker steps are CPU-heavy against the 10 ms limit: URL import with dom_smoothie readability in Worker wasm, parsing a whole book's segment index on upload and inserting thousands of D1 rows, base64 or byte-array audio for Whisper, and MeloTTS MP3 bytes passing through. Any of these can hit Error 1102. Pulling the text/import deps into the Worker also bloats the wasm.
issues.fix: The Worker fetches URLs only: it checks against SSRF and streams the raw HTML to the client, and the client runs dom_smoothie in browser wasm. Keep the segment index on the client. Have the render request carry the segment texts ({voice, items:[{idx,text}]}), so the Worker hashes small strings and never loads a book. Stream document bodies to R2 without parsing them, and keep only metadata in D1 (id, title, r2_key, segmenter_version, segment_count, progress). Drop Whisper from v1, because the guided clone script is the transcript. Drop MeloTTS from v1. Make sure the Worker crate never depends on the import crate.

issues.problem: The Worker–Space contract is unspecified. Gradio endpoints take positional data:[...] arrays, there is no schema version, and nothing defines per-item results or partial failure. Python 'contracts' and Rust DTOs will drift silently, and one bad segment can fail a whole GPU batch, wasting one of about 3 daily runs. Phase 2 (Kaggle or GitHub Actions bulk) would need yet another contract.
issues.fix: Give each Gradio endpoint one string input and one string output: render(request_json) -> result_json. The request is {v:1, engine, model_rev, voice:{kind, id, ref_key, ref_text}, items:[{key, text, spans}], out_prefix}. The result is {v:1, items:[{key, ok, duration_ms, words:[...], error:{code,msg}}]}. Define the types in Rust with serde + schemars. `cargo xtask schema` writes contracts/engine.v1.schema.json plus fixtures, and CI fails if they differ from what is committed. pytest validates the fixtures and the fake engine's output against the schema, and a Rust test deserialises Python-produced golden results. Have the GPU endpoint yield per item, so each item is uploaded and reported as soon as it finishes (still one scheduled run). Add a health endpoint returning {contract_version, engines:{name: model_rev}, git_sha}. The Worker checks it on cron and refuses on mismatch. Deploy order: Space first (accepting v and v-1), then Worker. Reuse the same JSON contract unchanged as the payload for the phase 2 bulk job.

issues.problem: Worker logic cannot be tested natively. workers-rs types (Env, D1Database, Bucket, Ai) exist only on wasm32, so routes, job orchestration, auth and the SSE client written directly against them can only be tested by deploying. The 'unit tests in worker logic' in the plan have no seam.
issues.fix: Split the logic into a native `server` crate. It holds the application services as plain async functions over small ?Send traits (Repo, Blob, Engine, Llm, JobQueue, Clock) and returns Result<Dto, ApiError>. The `worker` crate holds only the workers-rs adapters and the router. Test `server` with in-memory fakes, and test the SQL with a rusqlite-backed Repo that runs the real migrations/*.sql (D1 is SQLite). Test the Gradio SSE parser against recorded byte streams, including heartbeat, error and split-chunk cases.

issues.problem: The cache key sha256(engine, voice, settings, normalised text) is under-specified. It omits the model revision, the reference clip hash (re-recording 'my voice' keeps the voice id, so stale audio would be served), the director output or version, and the normaliser/segmenter version. It also gives no canonical byte encoding, so ad hoc string concatenation can collide or differ between implementations.
issues.fix: In core, define CacheKey::new(KeyInput{key_version, engine, model_rev, voice_fingerprint (preset id, or sha256 of the ref clip plus ref_text), settings (sorted, fixed-precision), director_fingerprint (span list hash or 'none'), normaliser_version, text}). Encode it with length-prefixed fields and lock it with golden tests. Only Rust computes keys, never Python. The web client uses the same function, so it can check its offline cache before calling the network.

issues.problem: Renders are not deduplicated. Two overlapping window requests (prefetch plus a seek, or a retry) render the same segments twice. On the GPU tier that wastes one of about 3 daily runs and part of the 5 minutes. Stuck-job recovery also has nothing to work from.
issues.fix: Add a D1 table renders(key PRIMARY KEY, status, attempt, lease_until, error_code, engine, created_at). Claim keys with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING, and enqueue only the newly claimed ones. The consumer extends the lease, and the cron re-enqueues expired leases up to N attempts. Add a gpu_ledger(ts, seconds, runs) table, and put the budget check in core as a pure function: refuse or downgrade an expressive request before spending a run when the rolling 24 h ledger shows it cannot fit.

issues.problem: There is no error taxonomy or fallback policy. ZeroGPU produces separate failures (runs limit, quota with retry time, illegal duration, Space asleep or building returning 503, auth 401), and the plan does not say how each is detected or what the app does. Python gr.Error text and the spaces wrapper messages reach the Worker as free text.
issues.fix: In core, define EngineError {RunsLimit, Quota{retry_after}, IllegalDuration, Sleeping, Busy, BadInput{item}, Auth, Internal}. Write one classifier for SSE error payloads and HTTP status, and test it against the exact spaces 0.51.3 strings. Define the policy in one place: Quota/RunsLimit switches the request to Kokoro and marks the segment upgradable; Sleeping retries with backoff while the cron wakes the Space; BadInput fails only that item. Give the HTTP API one ApiError body {code, message, retry_after} defined in the shared DTOs. Add Rust lints unwrap_used, expect_used and panic = deny in the Worker crates, because a wasm panic poisons the isolate.

issues.problem: The units for text offsets are undefined. Director spans use 'word offsets' and the Space returns word timings, but Rust String indexes are UTF-8 bytes, Python str indexes are code points, and the browser DOM uses UTF-16. Kokoro tokens are also post-G2P text ('Dr.' becomes 'Doctor'). Highlighting and tag insertion will misalign on any non-ASCII text, including curly quotes and Arabic.
issues.fix: Specify in the contract that all offsets are Unicode scalar indices into the exact item.text sent. The Space maps Kokoro tokens back to source ranges and returns words:[{start_ms, end_ms, cs, ce}], with an empty list when alignment fails (then the client falls back to sentence highlighting). The LLM emits director spans as word indices from core's tokenizer, which is more reliable than raw offsets; core converts them to scalar offsets and validates them (in range, non-overlapping, tag in the allowlist). Rendering spans into Ming's tag syntax happens in the Space's ming adapter, because the syntax is specific to that engine.

issues.problem: The scope is too large for tonight and for one user: four engine tiers, three Workers AI models, voice design, the director, a Queue, cron with three duties, plus Kaggle. Each extra moving part adds an untested path, while the parts that matter (job model, contract, tests) are under-specified.
issues.fix: Tonight's v1: Kokoro on the Space CPU through the single job path; Ming clone and expressive on the GPU behind a flag, with the director off by default; one cron (daily wake plus lease recovery). Defer MeloTTS, voice design, Whisper, the quota endpoint and Kaggle to phase 2, and record the deferral in 05-decisions. Keep the contract engine-agnostic so they plug in later without changing the Worker.

issues.problem: Space concurrency is unspecified. The research template uses demo.queue(default_concurrency_limit=1), which puts CPU and GPU endpoints in one queue. A long Kokoro book batch would block a clone render and the cron health ping, and torch thread count on 2 vCPU is unset.
issues.fix: Give render_cpu concurrency_id='cpu' with concurrency_limit=1 and torch.set_num_threads(2). Give render_gpu concurrency_id='gpu' with concurrency_limit=1. Make health a plain, unqueued route that never touches @spaces.GPU. Cap CPU batches by character count (constant in core) so one call returns within a few minutes.

issues.problem: D1 migration tracking in xtask is undefined. Without a ledger, re-running deploy re-applies or skips SQL unpredictably, and nothing checks that an applied migration was not edited.
issues.fix: Name migrations/NNNN_name.sql, forward-only. In xtask, create _migrations(id, name, sha256, applied_at), apply each pending file plus its ledger insert in one D1 /query batch (atomic), and fail if an applied file's checksum changed. Run the same files in the server crate's rusqlite tests.

issues.problem: Static asset delivery and version skew are open. include_bytes! couples every UI change to a Worker rebuild, and every asset request counts against Worker requests and CPU. Separately, an installed PWA with a cached old bundle can call a newer API.
issues.fix: In xtask, use Workers Static Assets through the upload session (manifest of hashes, bucket uploads, completion JWT in the same multipart script upload). Web and API then deploy atomically, assets are served without invoking the Worker, and not_found_handling='single-page-application' covers router fallback. Set run_worker_first for /api/*. Add an X-Nolabs-Api header checked by the Worker, returning 409 upgrade_required so the service worker reloads.

issues.problem: D5 allows TypeScript glue, but there is no Node, so tsc cannot type-check it. That leaves a TS build step with no benefit and an esbuild dependency in the web build.
issues.fix: Write interop/ as plain ES modules (player.js, media_session.js, pdf.js) with JSDoc types, and import them through #[wasm_bindgen(module = "/interop/player.js")]. Trunk bundles them with no extra build step. Keep the player state machine (queue, prefetch threshold, highlight index) in Rust, so it is natively testable.

issues.problem: Deploy credentials and secret handling in xtask are vague. The plan names the full-access Global API Key and a write-role HF token. Re-uploading the script can drop secrets, and there is no guard against touching non-nolabs resources.
issues.fix: In xtask, read ~/.config/streams/*.env at runtime and never write it to the repo. Pass keep_bindings:['secret_text'] and set secrets through the /secrets endpoint. Assert that every resource name starts with 'nolabs-' before any mutating call. Write resolved ids (D1 id, queue id) to a gitignored deploy/state.toml, using ensure semantics (find by name, else create). Give the Worker a fine-grained HF read token and the Space an R2 token scoped to nolabs-media. Publish the Space with `uvx --from huggingface_hub hf upload` (allowed by the uv rule) and set Space secrets through the HF API.

issues.problem: CI is not defined. Clippy and tests are listed, but no workflow enforces them or catches schema drift.
issues.fix: Add .github/workflows/ci.yml: cargo fmt --check; clippy -D warnings natively and for wasm32 (web, worker); cargo test (core, server, import with rusqlite); `cargo xtask schema && git diff --exit-code contracts/`; `uv run pytest space/tests` with fake engines; Swatinem/rust-cache. Deploy stays local through xtask tonight; add a manual-dispatch deploy.yml later with a scoped CF API token.

issues.problem: The proposed crate split puts importers and director span application in `text`, mixes wire DTOs with domain logic in `core`, and has no home for application services.
issues.fix: Cleanest layout. crates/core: pure, no I/O; modules ids, proto (HTTP DTOs, engine contract v1, ApiError; schemars behind a feature), text (normaliser, segmenter with SEGMENTER_VERSION, word tokenizer), cache_key, director (span validation), engine_error (classifier), budget (batching, GPU ledger math), job (claim/lease state machine); proptest plus golden tests. crates/import: EPUB (zip + quick-xml), HTML (dom_smoothie), MD, TXT; web only. crates/server: services over the Repo, Blob, Engine, Llm, JobQueue and Clock traits, plus fakes and rusqlite repo for tests. crates/worker: workers-rs adapters, router, Gradio SSE transport, cookie auth, queue/cron entry points. crates/web: Leptos app/, pages/, components/, player/ (pure state machine), api.rs (core::proto), interop/*.js. xtask: build, deploy/{cf,assets,d1,secrets}, space, schema, smoke. contracts/ (generated schema plus fixtures). migrations/. space/: app.py (wiring only), nolabs_engine/{contract,engines/{base,kokoro,ming},audio,storage,errors}.py, vendor/ming, tests/. Six Rust crates is the minimum that keeps every piece of logic natively testable, which matters for one user who will not review code.

reviews.lens: Audio and TTS quality engineering (segmentation, prosody continuity, boundary gaps, Kokoro voices, Ming task usage, LLM director, loudness, Opus, word timing, cache keys, expressiveness per GPU second)
strengths: Kokoro on the Space CPU as default narrator and Ming on the GPU for clone and expressive work is the right split for a 5 GPU-min/day, 3-runs/day budget.
Director returns structured annotations instead of rewritten text, so the source cannot drift; validation is planned in Rust.
Static gain instead of loudnorm compression, measured with an EBU R128 meter, follows correction 3 in principle.
One batched GPU call per job respects the run-count limit; the Space writes straight to R2 so the Worker does not touch audio bytes on the primary path.
Designed voices become a fixed reference clip and are then used like clones, which avoids timbre drift between VOICE_DESIGN calls.
Ogg Opus with Range support, a 5 s minimum clip, and content-addressed cache keys are a sound base.

issues.problem: Ming cannot run the director contract as written (one emotion label plus paralinguistic tags per segment, sent to render_gpu). The Ming README says each call selects one task and 'controls from another task are rejected'. Tags work in the TTS task, which takes prompt_wav and prompt_text. EMOTION takes a reference clip, no prompt_text, and only the `emotion` control. IP takes only `ip`. FREEFORM takes only `instruction`. The emotion values are the Chinese strings 高兴/悲伤/愤怒/恐惧/厌恶/惊讶/中性, so English labels passed through would be rejected too.
issues.fix: Have the director output one `mode` per Ming segment from {tts_plain, tts_tags, emotion}, plus an English emotion enum {happy, sad, angry, fearful, disgusted, surprised, neutral}. Only the Python adapter maps that enum to the Chinese strings. In Rust, reject `tags` unless mode is tts_tags and reject `emotion` unless mode is emotion. Add a Python contract test that runs one tiny call per mode against the real model before deploy.

issues.problem: The catalogue claims Ming built-in voices come 'with emotion variants'. Checked against cookbooks/instruction_en.md on 2026-10-30, there are only three English IP voices (US_Emma, UK_George, UK_Charlotte) and none has emotion variants; the variant table covers Chinese voices only. The IP task also cannot take emotion or tags.
issues.fix: List three English Ming presets. To make them expressive, run one GPU job per preset: render a 10-15 s neutral passage with IP, save it plus its exact text as a reference, then render the same voice through EMOTION with that reference for happy, sad, angry and fearful. Save each as a labelled reference excerpt. From then on, IP voices are handled like clones (TTS task plus tags, with the reference matched to the emotion). Correct note 06 and the catalogue.

issues.problem: Per-segment −18 LUFS normalisation undoes the expressive dynamics between segments. A whispered sad paragraph is raised to the level of a shouted angry one. Correction 3 asked for one static gain toward a chapter target, not a target per segment. The plan also has no true-peak ceiling, so positive gain can clip, and Opus decoding overshoots above 0 dBFS. −18 LUFS is also quiet on a phone speaker.
issues.fix: Calibrate one gain per (engine, voice, reference excerpt) on a fixed 60 s calibration passage, targeting −16 LUFS integrated, and store it with the voice. Per segment, apply that gain plus a correction of at most ±2 dB toward −16 LUFS for Ming (±4 dB for Kokoro, which is flat anyway). Then cap the gain so the sample peak stays at or below −1.5 dBFS (true peak −1 dBTP), with no limiter. Pass the gain to ffmpeg with `-af volume=XdB`.

issues.problem: Clip boundaries have uncontrolled gaps. The gap between clips is the trailing silence of clip A, plus the leading silence of clip B, plus the src-switch latency of one audio element (assumed tens to hundreds of ms in note 03). This makes sentence rhythm uneven at every boundary, and the ear notices it more than a slightly wrong pause length. Ogg Opus also cannot be fed to MSE on Chrome, so gapless playback can't be added later without re-encoding the cache.
issues.fix: In the Space, trim leading and trailing silence (threshold −45 dBFS, keep a 30 ms guard), apply 5 ms fades, then append a deterministic pause by boundary type. Set the sentence pause to the median intra-segment sentence pause measured on a Kokoro test chapter (silencedetect), use about 2x that for paragraphs and 1.5 s for headings or scene breaks. Store the boundary type in the segment row. Encode WebM Opus (`-f webm`) instead of Ogg, and play through MSE with SourceBuffer mode `sequence` on the same audio element: it is gapless, and the media notification still works. Keep one-element src switching only as a fallback.

issues.problem: Segments of 150–600 characters exceed Kokoro's sweet spot. VOICES.md says voices work best at 100–200 tokens and rush above 400 tokens, out of 510. 600 English characters is roughly 450–550 phoneme tokens, so KPipeline splits at arbitrary points or the voice rushes. For Ming, the reverse applies: longer, paragraph-sized inputs keep prosody continuous within a call, while each call restarts pitch declination.
issues.fix: Use segment limits per engine in nolabs-text. Kokoro: 120–320 characters, never split inside a sentence, no newlines inside the segment (KPipeline splits on \n+). Ming: one whole paragraph per call, up to about 500 characters; longer paragraphs split at the sentence boundary closest to the middle. Make segmentation a function of engine in the segment index, and include the segmenter version in the cache key.

issues.problem: The plan drops the ASR check that both chats agreed on. Ming 0.5b is an autoregressive LM with a DiT head; skipped or repeated words would only be noticed while listening. A re-render costs a new GPU run, and the account gets 3 per day. Ming word timing is also deferred to phase 2, so expressive playback has no highlighting tonight.
issues.fix: Load whisper-large-v3-turbo (transformers 4.46.3, `pipeline(..., return_timestamps='word')`) on cuda at module level next to Ming. Inside the same @spaces.GPU call: render, transcribe, and compute WER against the normalised text. When WER is above 8% or the last 3 words are missing, re-render once with a different seed in the same call. If it fails again, mark the segment for the Kokoro paired voice. Return the word timestamps as the highlight manifest. This costs a few GPU seconds per audio minute and no extra runs.

issues.problem: The director design asks a 26B LLM for 'paralinguistic tags at word offsets'. LLMs miscount character and word offsets, and without anchoring a wrong offset puts a tag in the wrong place or splits a word. The plan also has no tag whitelist for English, no density cap, and no handling of source text that already contains brackets. Wikipedia-style [1] citations and stray [Sigh] in imported text would reach Ming, where tags are case-sensitive and bypass normalisation.
issues.fix: Schema: one entry per sentence, each `{sentence_idx, mode, emotion, confidence, tags:[{before_word_idx, anchor_word, tag}]}`. Rust checks that words[before_word_idx] == anchor_word. On a mismatch it searches ±3 words for the anchor, and drops the tag if not found. Allowed English tags: [Breathing] [Sigh] [Laughter] [Surprise-ah] [Surprise-oh] [Uhm] [Cough]. Exclude the Mandarin-interjection tags (Confirmation-en, Question-*, Dissatisfaction-hnn). At most 1 tag per sentence and 2 per segment; Ming's README says multi-tag stability trails single-tag. None in non-fiction. In normalisation, remove [digits] citations and turn any other '[' ']' in source text into parentheses. Send the previous and next paragraph as read-only context.

issues.problem: The plan doesn't account for Ming's weakness on emotion. The README says emotion accuracy drops when the words carry no emotional signal, and the plan doesn't say how the director's labels should account for that. Applied per segment without smoothing, emotion labels make delivery swing from one paragraph to the next. EMOTION mode also drops prompt_text, which likely lowers speaker similarity compared with the TTS task (assumed).
issues.fix: Default to tts_plain or tts_tags using an emotion-matched reference excerpt; the excerpt is the strongest lever, because Ming copies prosody from the prompt. Use EMOTION mode only when director confidence is at least 0.75 and the sentence is in quoted dialogue. Apply hysteresis: change emotion at most once per 3 sentences, and keep narration neutral. Ming segments are grouped from consecutive sentences with the same (mode, emotion, excerpt), so a segment never mixes emotions.

issues.problem: The clone reference plan (record 20–60 s and save {ref_key, transcript}) uses the whole clip as prompt_wav for every call. Long prompts add prompt tokens to every segment and tend to hurt zero-shot cloning; one neutral prompt also limits expressiveness. On Android Chrome, getUserMedia applies AGC, noise suppression and echo cancellation by default, which smears the timbre the model copies.
issues.fix: Record with getUserMedia constraints {echoCancellation:false, noiseSuppression:false, autoGainControl:false, channelCount:1}. Upload lossless audio: WAV built from PCM in an AudioWorklet, or Opus at 128 kbps or more if size matters. Run the guided script with labelled lines (neutral, warm, sad, tense, excited). Cut 6–12 s excerpts per label using Whisper word timestamps, so each excerpt's transcript is exact. Store the voice as {spk_emb_from_neutral, excerpts:{label:{key, text}}}. Pick the excerpt by director emotion and use the TTS task.

issues.problem: The cache key sha256(engine, voice, settings, normalised text) leaves out inputs that change the audio. Re-recording a voice keeps the same voice id, so the cache serves the old timbre. Updating the model or Space code silently mixes old and new renders inside one chapter.
issues.fix: Hash a versioned canonical struct, encoded with serde_json with sorted keys or postcard with length-prefixed fields: {key_version, engine, model_repo@commit_sha, adapter_version, voice_id, reference_excerpt_sha256, kokoro_lang_code, speed, ming_mode, emotion, tags_hash, normaliser_version, segmenter_version, boundary_pause_ms, codec_profile_id (container/bitrate/rate), loudness_profile_id, text}. Leave the seed out of the key and store the accepted seed in the manifest. The director cache key is {model_id, prompt_version, schema_version, paragraph_text, context_hash}.

issues.problem: Kokoro word timestamps need offset bookkeeping the plan does not mention. KPipeline yields one Result per internal chunk, with token start_ts/end_ts relative to that chunk. Silence trimming and appended pauses shift time. Misaki token text after Rust normalisation does not map to the char offsets of the displayed source. Highlighting driven by timeupdate (about 4 Hz on Android) also lags word by word.
issues.fix: In the Space, add a cumulative chunk offset, subtract the trimmed leading silence, and emit [{char_start, char_end, t_ms_start, t_ms_end}] against the segment's original text. Get the offsets by aligning misaki tokens to the source sequentially in Rust, using the offset map nolabs-text keeps through normalisation. In the app, poll currentTime with requestAnimationFrame while the page is visible. Media time already accounts for playbackRate, so no scaling is needed.

issues.problem: With 3 runs a day and 5 GPU-minutes, the GPU window also contains steps that don't need a GPU: ffmpeg encoding, loudness measurement and R2 uploads, if done inside the decorated function. A batch whose requested duration ×1.5 exceeds the remaining quota is refused outright, and a timeout loses every segment of the batch.
issues.fix: Write the @spaces.GPU function as a generator that yields (segment_id, pcm_float32, words, wer) per segment. The calling CPU-side code does trimming, gain, encoding and the R2 upload as each item arrives. Set duration with a callable: measured_rtf × estimated_audio_s + 15 s. Measure RTF on the first run and store it in D1. If requested_s × 1.5 would exceed remaining quota, cut the batch to fit and queue the rest.

issues.problem: Opus at 24 kHz throws away Ming's 44.1 kHz output above 12 kHz, the 'air' that makes it sound premium on headphones. The plan also gives no application mode or resampler.
issues.fix: Ming: `-af aresample=48000:resampler=soxr -c:a libopus -b:a 56k -vbr on -application audio -compression_level 10 -frame_duration 20`. Kokoro (24 kHz native): the same flags at `-b:a 32k`. Store the profile id in the cache key.

issues.problem: Exposing all 28 English Kokoro voices offers mostly C/D/F grade voices (am_adam F+, several D). The catalogue looks large but most voices sound poor, and the male voices are weak.
issues.fix: Show af_heart (default), af_bella, af_nicole, bf_emma, am_michael, am_fenrir, am_puck, bm_george and bm_fable. Hide the rest behind 'more'. Create one KPipeline per lang_code ('a', 'b') at module level. For a premium male narrator, point users to Ming UK_George with the paired reference.

issues.problem: The plan doesn't say how Kokoro and Ming voices combine within one document. If expressive segments interleave with Kokoro narration, the timbre jumps at every switch.
issues.fix: Pair each Kokoro voice with a Ming reference cloned from 12 s of that Kokoro voice reading neutral text, using the exact transcript and calibrated to the same LUFS. Switch engines only at paragraph or scene boundaries, or for whole quoted-dialogue paragraphs. Spend GPU seconds on dialogue-heavy paragraphs and keep narration on Kokoro. Listen to an A/B before enabling it by default.

issues.problem: Time to first audio is long. The first window goes to render_cpu as one call on 2 vCPU, and the Worker waits for the full SSE completion before playback.
issues.fix: Render the first segment alone (shortest, at least 5 s) and report each completed segment as a separate SSE `generating` event with its manifest row. The app starts on the first one while the rest of the window renders.

issues.problem: MeloTTS fallback output arrives in the Worker. Decoding or re-encoding it breaks the 10 ms CPU budget, and it gets no loudness matching, so a fallback window plays at a different level and timbre.
issues.fix: Use the fallback per window, never per segment. Pass the Workers AI audio payload to the client without decoding it in the Worker. Measure Melo's typical LUFS once, and if it is louder than −16 LUFS, attenuate with audio.volume (which can only reduce). Show a 'basic voice' badge while it plays, and never write it under a primary-engine cache key.

strengths: Single origin with an HttpOnly, Secure, SameSite=Strict cookie, and every /api route requires it. Same origin means no CORS is needed and there is no token in JS reach.
The private Space plus a server-held HF token means only the Worker (and the owner) can spend the 5 GPU-min quota. Anonymous callers of a private Space cannot reach the endpoints.
Secrets live in Worker/Space secret stores, never in the repo or notes, and note 04 records locations only.
The director emits structured spans that are validated against the source, so prompt injection hidden in imported text cannot change the words read aloud.
Worker static assets are served without invoking the Worker, so an attacker loading the app shell does not consume the 100k/day request budget.
All new resources use the nolabs- prefix, and note 04 lists the resources that must not be touched, which makes a scoped guard easy to write.

issues.problem: xtask deploys with the Cloudflare Global API Key (raw research deploy snippet uses X-Auth-Email/X-Auth-Key everywhere). That key has full rights over the whole account: the 15 existing Workers, bucket pstream-data, the streams.watch DNS zone and Pages projects. A bug in xtask, such as a wrong name in a DELETE or PUT, or a leaked env file, can destroy unrelated production resources.
issues.fix: Add `xtask bootstrap-token`, the only code path that ever reads the Global key. It calls POST /user/tokens once to mint a 'nolabs-deploy' API token limited to this account: Workers Scripts Edit, Workers R2 Storage Edit, D1 Edit, Queues Edit, Workers Tail Read, plus Zone Workers Routes Edit and DNS Edit only on zone streams.watch (needed only when the custom domain is attached). Set expires_on to 90 days. Write it to ~/.config/nolabs/cloudflare-deploy.env with mode 600. All other xtask commands use `Authorization: Bearer` and refuse to start if only X-Auth-Key is present. Tokens cannot be scoped to named Workers or buckets, so xtask also hard-codes an allowlist: any mutating request whose script, bucket, database or queue name does not start with `nolabs-` panics before it is sent, and xtask has no delete subcommands for non-nolabs resources. That POST /user/tokens accepts Global API Key auth is assumed. If it is refused, the user creates the same token in the dashboard (about 2 minutes), and the note records the permission list.

issues.problem: 'HF token' in Worker secrets is unspecified, and the only HF token on record (note 04) has role write over every repo, including streams-engine. Putting it in the Worker gives a long-lived write credential to an internet-facing service. The research snippet also sends it as a plain Authorization header, which reaches the Space app process (raw research line 797/827), where logs or vendored code can see it.
issues.fix: Create a fine-grained HF token 'nolabs-worker' with read access only to the repo ibrahimar397/nolabs-engine (plus 'Read billing usage' so the cron can call GET /api/spaces/zero-gpu/quota). Store it only as the Worker secret HF_TOKEN. The write token stays on the Mac for `hf upload` and is never placed in any Space or Worker. Before go-live, measure attribution: run hf spaces zero-gpu quota, make one GPU call with the fine-grained token in x-hf-authorization, run quota again, then repeat with Authorization: Bearer. Keep x-hf-authorization if it debits the account's 5 min, since the proxy strips it before the app. Record the result in note 03. The Space itself needs no HF token, because Kokoro and Ming weights are ungated.

issues.problem: R2 S3 keys sit in Space secrets. The default R2 API token is account-wide, Admin Read & Write, which would let code in the Space read, overwrite or delete pstream-data. The Space runs a large third-party Python stack (vendored Ming, spacy, misaki, transformers, ffmpeg) with those keys in its environment.
issues.fix: Remove R2 credentials from the Space entirely. The Worker presigns S3 SigV4 URLs (a few HMAC-SHA256 operations per URL, well under 10 ms CPU): one PUT URL per output object (fixed key audio/<voice_id>/<hash>.opus, fixed Content-Type audio/ogg, expiry 15 min), plus one GET URL for a voice reference clip when needed. These go in the render_cpu/render_gpu request. The S3 keys used for presigning are an R2 token limited to bucket nolabs-media with Object Read & Write, held only as Worker secrets. If presigning is deferred, at minimum mint the Space token as Object Read & Write on nolabs-media only, never Admin.

issues.problem: The reader renders imported content (HTML from arbitrary URLs, EPUB XHTML, Markdown, PDF via pdf.js) on the same origin that holds the session. v1 says nothing about sanitising or CSP. A script in an imported article or EPUB, or a malicious PDF (pdf.js before 4.2.67, CVE-2024-4367, runs arbitrary JS via font matrices), would run with full API access: it could read every document, download the voice reference clip, delete data or burn quota. HttpOnly does not stop same-origin fetches.
issues.fix: 1) nolabs-text outputs plain text segments only (no HTML survives import), and Leptos renders them as text nodes. Ban inner_html in crates/web with clippy's disallowed_methods. 2) The Worker sets on every HTML response: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'none'; script-src 'self' 'wasm-unsafe-eval'; style-src 'self'; img-src 'self' data: blob:; media-src 'self' blob:; connect-src 'self'; worker-src 'self'; manifest-src 'self'; font-src 'self'; base-uri 'none'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors 'none'. Also set X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff and Referrer-Policy: no-referrer. For static assets use an _headers file. 3) Pin pdfjs-dist at 4.2.67 or later, self-host it, and call getDocument with isEvalSupported: false. 4) EPUB import caps total uncompressed size (for example 200 MB) and the per-entry ratio, to avoid zip bombs crashing the A12-class tab.

issues.problem: Login is a passphrase with no stated strength or rate limit. Free Workers cannot run Argon2/bcrypt within 10 ms CPU, so slow hashing is not available, and the login route is reachable by anyone on workers.dev and the custom domain.
issues.fix: xtask generates the secret instead of the user choosing one: 128 random bits shown once as 26 base32 characters, or 10 EFF diceware words. The Worker stores HMAC-SHA256(SESSION_KEY, passphrase) as a secret and compares in constant time, so brute force is infeasible without slow hashing. Add a global failure counter in D1: after 20 failed logins in an hour, return 429 for an hour. On the custom domain, use the one free WAF rate limiting rule on /api/login (for example 5 requests per 10 s per IP, block 10 s). Save the passphrase for the smoke test in ~/.config/nolabs/app.env, mode 600.

issues.problem: The stateless HMAC cookie lasts 180 days and has no revocation. If the phone is lost or the cookie is copied, the only remedy is undocumented. The cookie also lacks a __Host- prefix. Once the app moves to listen.streams.watch, any other streams.watch subdomain (Pages sites, other Workers) can set a Domain=.streams.watch cookie with the same name and force a login or shadow the session (cookie tossing).
issues.fix: Name the cookie __Host-nolabs_s with Path=/ and no Domain. Signed payload = {sid, issued_at, expires_at, epoch}; the Worker checks expires_at on the server, not just Max-Age. Keep a D1 config row session_epoch; `xtask revoke-sessions` (or POST /api/logout-all) increments it, which invalidates every cookie with a single D1 read per request. Add a sliding refresh: reissue when under 30 days remain.

issues.problem: CSRF defences rest only on SameSite=Strict. The research Worker skeleton enables CORS with origins '*' and allows the authorization header. Copying it would make the API readable from other origins whenever a request needs no cookie (login, health), and it widens the attack surface for no benefit on a single origin.
issues.fix: Remove the Cors middleware entirely and answer OPTIONS with 405. For every non-GET /api route, require Content-Type: application/json, and reject the request unless Sec-Fetch-Site is same-origin or the Origin header equals the deployed origin. A unit test in crates/worker covers each case.

issues.problem: The workers.dev URL stays public after the custom domain is attached. It bypasses zone WAF and rate limiting, so anyone can hit the Worker there to exhaust the shared 100k requests/day (for the whole account, including the other 15 Workers) or brute force login without the WAF rule. Preview URLs add another unprotected origin.
issues.fix: After the custom domain is live and the smoke test passes, xtask calls POST /workers/scripts/nolabs-api/subdomain with {enabled:false, previews_enabled:false}. Until then, the login route on workers.dev keeps the D1 lockout from the passphrase fix. Add a D1 per-day request counter that the cron reports in the quota report.

issues.problem: The URL fetcher rule 'refuses private-network addresses' targets a risk that barely exists on Workers: fetch() egresses from Cloudflare's edge, and DNS cannot be resolved in a Worker, so a hostname check does not stop DNS rebinding. The real risks are unchecked: redirects to other schemes or hosts, unbounded body size against the 128 MB memory and 10 ms CPU limits, and forwarding credentials.
issues.fix: In the fetcher: allow only http/https on ports 80/443; parse with the url crate and reject literal IPs in loopback, RFC1918, link-local (169.254/16, fe80::/10), CGNAT 100.64/10, ULA fc00::/7 and v4-mapped v6; reject localhost, *.local, *.internal and the app's own hostnames. Use redirect: manual, revalidate each Location, max 5 hops. Send a fixed User-Agent and no Cookie or Authorization headers. Read the body as a stream with a hard 5 MB cap and a 15 s timeout, and accept only text/html, application/xhtml+xml, text/plain, text/markdown or application/epub+zip. The Space never accepts URLs to fetch: Gradio file inputs given as {path: URL} make the Space download them, so the Space validates that any URL host is <account>.r2.cloudflarestorage.com with a presigned query, and rejects anything else.

issues.problem: GET /api/audio/{key} streams from R2 by key, and the bucket also holds document bodies and voice reference clips. A key with slashes or another prefix could serve the voice clip or documents through the audio route. The bucket's public r2.dev access state is not specified.
issues.fix: The route accepts only [0-9a-f]{64} (and an optional voice_id segment matching the voice id format), then reads exactly audio/<voice_id>/<hash>.opus. Voice clips are fetched only by voice id through D1, under the voices/ prefix. xtask asserts on every deploy that r2.dev public access is disabled on nolabs-media (GET /r2/buckets/nolabs-media/domains/managed returns enabled:false), that no custom domain and no CORS policy are set, and fails the deploy otherwise.

issues.problem: Voice recordings have no retention or deletion design. They are the data that would let someone else clone the user's voice. The cache key sha256(engine, voice, settings, text) is flat, so deleting a voice cannot find its rendered audio. Raw takes, Gradio temp files on the Space disk and Queue messages may keep copies.
issues.fix: Store only the trimmed reference clip at voices/<voice_id>/ref.opus and delete the raw recording after the user accepts the trim. Prefix rendered audio with the voice id (audio/<voice_id>/<hash>.opus) so DELETE /api/voices/{id} removes the D1 row, the reference clip and every rendered segment via list+delete by prefix, and records the deletion in D1. On the Space, load the reference from the presigned GET into memory or a temp file deleted in a finally block. Return no Gradio file outputs, and set Blocks(delete_cache=(3600, 3600)). Queue messages carry ids only, never text or URLs. Log only ids and durations in Worker and Space logs. Phase 2 Kaggle: pass presigned URLs in a private dataset manifest, never R2 keys or the clip in a public dataset.

issues.problem: An authenticated client bug (render loop, prefetch storm) or a stuck job retry can drain the day's 5 GPU-min and 10k Workers AI neurons. The design has no server-side spending caps. The keepalive cron could also hit a GPU endpoint by mistake.
issues.fix: Keep daily budget counters in D1: GPU seconds requested (from the duration sent to @spaces.GPU), Workers AI neurons (estimated from tokens and audio minutes), and Space calls. render_gpu and director calls are refused with 429 'budget' when the configured cap is reached (for example 280 GPU-s and 8,000 neurons). Queue max_retries 1 for GPU jobs. Cron keepalive calls only the CPU health endpoint, and a test asserts that health has no @spaces.GPU decorator.

issues.problem: Supply chain on the Space: model weights are loaded by name from HF at startup, so a later upstream change to inclusionAI/Ming-3.0-tts-0.5B or hexgrad/Kokoro-82M (new files, a pickle-based checkpoint) would run in the Space without review. The research deploy snippet also places secrets on curl command lines, where they appear in ps output and shell history.
issues.fix: Pin every from_pretrained / hf_hub_download to a commit sha (revision=...), load only .safetensors where available, and pass weights_only=True for any torch.load. Install from the verified lock with exact versions. In xtask, secrets are read from the env file into secrecy::SecretString, sent in request bodies via reqwest (never argv), set through PUT /workers/scripts/{name}/secrets, and preserved on uploads with keep_bindings: ["secret_text"]. Any error output that would echo request bodies is redacted.

changes.change: Split tonight into two milestones, each written as a checklist in the plan note. Milestone A must pass on the A12 before any Milestone B work starts. A: paste, URL and EPUB import; Kokoro playback; gapless playback; 20 minutes screen-off with the app installed and no gap over 300 ms; notification and Bluetooth controls; resume; speed control; sleep timer; rolling offline cache. B: clone, Ming, quota UX. Defer MeloTTS, Workers AI Whisper, voice design, the director, the HF quota endpoint and Kaggle to phase 2, and record this in 05-decisions as D6. If the screen-off check fails after Samsung battery exemptions (Settings > Apps > Chrome > Battery > Unrestricted, and removal from Sleeping/Deep sleeping apps), move the native Android shell up from phase 3.
changes.reason: All five reviews flag tonight's scope as too large, and nothing in v1 is tested on the phone. Goal 1 (listening with the screen off) is the product. Where the architecture reviewer (cut) and the UX reviewer (add features) conflict, the architecture reviewer wins on scope and the UX reviewer wins on what Milestone A contains.

changes.change: Measure before building, in this order. (a) Create the Space with POST /api/repos/create (hardware zero-a10g) as step one. If that is blocked, Standard runs on a GitHub Actions Kokoro renderer writing to R2. (b) Measure Kokoro RTF on the deployed Space with 1,000 characters, and set the prefetch depth to 3x playback speed / RTF. (c) Spend at most 2 real GPU runs: one Ming RTF measurement on about 600 characters, and one end-to-end job. Leave the probe for a 4th call until tomorrow, because the reset is rolling 24 h. (d) Add a DEVICE=cpu switch so Ming 0.5B runs one sentence on CPU for contract and smoke tests that use no quota. (e) Read current account usage through the Cloudflare GraphQL analytics API (workers invocations, R2 storage including pstream-data). Record every number in note 03.
changes.reason: The feasibility, audio and UX reviewers agree that chunk sizes, prefetch depth and daily expressive minutes all depend on unmeasured RTFs. Testing carelessly can use up the 3 daily runs and block retesting for 24 h.

changes.change: Use one asynchronous render path for both tiers. POST /api/render receives segment texts from the client, computes keys, and claims misses in a D1 renders(key PK, status, attempt, lease_until, error_code) table with INSERT ... ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING RETURNING. It enqueues only newly claimed keys (batch_size 1) and returns {key,status} at once. The Queue consumer calls the Space. render_cpu and render_gpu are generators that yield one result per segment. For each segment the Space uploads audio/<voice_id>/<hash>.webm plus a sidecar <hash>.json (duration, timings, boundary type), so R2 is the source of truth and D1 can be rebuilt from it. The client GETs /api/audio/{key} and retries a 404 with backoff (1 s, then 2, 4, up to 15 s), never fixed 2 s polling. On import, enqueue the first 3 minutes immediately and the rest of the document in 20-segment messages, so play is usually a cache hit. On a cold play, the first message is one segment of 150 characters or fewer.
changes.reason: The architecture, feasibility and UX reviewers all flag the synchronous Standard path. Android drops the request with the screen off, waitUntil gives only 30 s, and the manifest is lost. The architecture reviewer's queue design wins over the feasibility reviewer's NDJSON stream held on the phone's request, because nothing should depend on the phone's connection staying open. Pre-rendering on import (from the feasibility and UX reviews) removes the extra queue latency from first play.

changes.change: Make playback gapless. The Space encodes WebM/Opus (-f webm), not Ogg. The client plays through MediaSource with one SourceBuffer of type 'audio/webm;codecs=opus' in mode 'sequence', one timeline per chapter, at least 3 minutes buffered ahead. Use navigator.mediaSession with MediaMetadata (title, chapter, cover at 512 px) and setPositionState for the chapter. seekbackward/seekforward move ±15 s, and previoustrack/nexttrack move by paragraph. In the Space: trim leading and trailing silence at -45 dBFS with a 30 ms guard and 5 ms fades, then append a fixed pause by boundary type (sentence = the measured median Kokoro intra-segment pause, paragraph = 2x that, heading or scene break = 1.5 s). Keep switching src on one audio element only as a fallback when isTypeSupported fails.
changes.reason: The UX reviewer rated this a blocker and the audio reviewer rated it major. Both are right: Chrome's MSE does not take Ogg, so v1's cache format would block gapless playback later. Fixed pauses also remove the uneven rhythm at every boundary.

changes.change: Keep the Worker within 10 ms of CPU. The client parses all imports (EPUB, HTML through dom_smoothie in browser wasm, MD, TXT) and segments them. The Worker's URL fetcher only fetches: http/https on ports 80/443 only, redirect manual with each Location revalidated (max 5 hops), a 5 MB streamed cap, a 15 s timeout, a content-type allowlist, and no Cookie or Authorization headers forwarded. Document bodies stream to R2 unparsed (FixedLengthStream). The segment index is one R2 JSON object per document. D1 holds only documents, progress, voices, renders, jobs and the ledgers. Look up cache hits for a window with one SELECT ... WHERE key IN (...), and group writes in db.batch(). The worker crate never depends on the import crate.
changes.reason: Three reviewers independently found Error 1102 risks: readability in the Worker, thousands of D1 inserts per book, and base64 audio. The security reviewer is right that a private-address check alone is weak in a Worker, so the fetcher gets the full rule set.

changes.change: Define the Worker-Space contract v1. Each Gradio endpoint takes one JSON string and returns one: request {v:1, engine, model_rev, voice:{kind,id,ref_url,ref_text}, items:[{key,text,mode,emotion,tags,boundary}], put_urls:{key:url}}. Each item result is {key, ok, duration_ms, words, error:{code,msg}}, so one bad item fails only itself. Rust types use serde and schemars, and `cargo xtask schema` writes contracts/engine.v1.schema.json plus fixtures that pytest validates. Add a /health route that is not queued, has no @spaces.GPU, and returns {contract_version, engines, git_sha, storage_ok}. Give render_cpu concurrency_id 'cpu' (limit 1, torch.set_num_threads(2)) and render_gpu concurrency_id 'gpu' (limit 1). In core, define EngineError {RunsLimit, Quota{retry_after}, IllegalDuration, Sleeping, Busy, BadInput{item}, Auth, Internal}, with a classifier tested against the exact spaces 0.51.3 strings and a single ApiError body {code,message,retry_after}. Deny unwrap_used, expect_used and panic in the worker crates.
changes.reason: The architecture reviewer showed that positional data arrays with no version will drift silently and that one bad segment can waste a GPU run. A per-item result and a single error taxonomy give fallback behaviour a single place to live.

changes.change: Protect the GPU budget. The GPU queue uses max_retries=0. The job row is written with state 'submitted' and deterministic output keys before the call. The Space writes jobs/{job_id}.json to R2 when it finishes, and the consumer and cron check that marker before any resubmit. 'runs limit' and 'quota' errors set state 'deferred' with retry_at taken from the error text. Keep a gpu_ledger(ts, requested_s, runs) table, with a pure budget function in core that refuses or shrinks a batch when requested_s x 1.5 exceeds the remaining rolling 24 h quota. duration = measured_rtf x estimated_audio_s x 1.3 + 15 s. The @spaces.GPU function yields float32 PCM only; trimming, gain, encoding and upload run outside it on CPU. Set a server cap of 280 GPU-s/day. The UI shows runs and seconds left before any GPU action. When quota runs out mid-document, playback continues in a Kokoro stand-in voice chosen at clone time, with a one-line notice.
changes.reason: The feasibility, architecture, audio and security reviewers each found a different way to burn one of the 3 daily runs: retries, duplicate renders, encoding inside the GPU window, and a prefetch storm. On retries, the feasibility reviewer's max_retries=0 plus a completion marker wins over the security reviewer's max_retries=1, because a retry cannot know whether the first Gradio job still succeeded.

changes.change: Specify the cache key and units in core. CacheKey::new(KeyInput{key_version, engine, model_repo@sha, adapter_version, voice_fingerprint (preset id, or sha256 of ref clip + ref_text), lang_code, ming_mode, emotion, tags_hash, normaliser_version, segmenter_version, boundary_pause_ms, codec_profile_id, loudness_profile_id, text}) is length-prefixed, locked by golden tests, and computed only in Rust, on both the Worker and the web client. Speed and seed are excluded; the accepted seed is stored in the sidecar. All text offsets are Unicode scalar indices into the exact item.text. Progress is stored as (doc_id, char_offset, updated_at): written to IndexedDB every 5 s and on pause, and synced with sendBeacon on visibilitychange=hidden, on pause and every 30 s. Resume starts one sentence before the saved offset.
