changes.reason: The architecture, audio and UX reviewers converged on this. v1's key serves stale audio after a re-record or model update. A progress value in seconds breaks across voices and tiers, and byte, UTF-16 and code-point offsets misalign on curly quotes and Arabic.

changes.change: Correct the Ming integration to match the vendored code. Each call picks one task, and tts_tasks.build_task_instruction rejects controls from other tasks (verified in space/vendor/ming3/tts_tasks.py). The adapter takes mode in {tts (prompt_wav + prompt_text, optional tags), ip (ip only), emotion (reference + emotion only)}. An English enum {happy,sad,angry,fearful,disgusted,surprised,neutral} is mapped to 高兴/悲伤/愤怒/恐惧/厌恶/惊讶/中性 only in Python. Rust rejects tags unless the mode is tts and rejects emotion unless the mode is emotion. Correct the catalogue: English IP voices are US_Emma, US_James and UK_George/UK_Charlotte (EN_IP_VOICES), and voices.json also lists US_Stella. All have empty variant lists, so there are no emotion variants. Add one CPU-mode contract test per mode.
changes.reason: The audio reviewer's blocker is confirmed in source, so v1's director-to-render_gpu contract would raise ValueError. The reviewer's count of 3 English voices is wrong: the vendored code lists 4 in EN_IP_VOICES and 5 in voices.json.

changes.change: Audio levels and encoding. Calibrate one gain per (engine, voice, reference) on a fixed 60 s passage, targeting -16 LUFS, and store it with the voice. Per segment, apply that gain plus a correction of at most ±2 dB (Ming) or ±4 dB (Kokoro), then cap the gain so the sample peak stays at or below -1.5 dBFS, with no limiter. Kokoro segments are 120-320 characters, never split inside a sentence and with no newlines. Ming gets one paragraph of up to about 500 characters per call. Encoding: Kokoro libopus 32k; Ming aresample=48000:resampler=soxr at 56k; both -application audio -vbr on -frame_duration 20, with the profile id in the cache key.
changes.reason: Per-segment -18 LUFS breaks correction 3 in note 02 and flattens expressive range between segments. Kokoro's VOICES.md says voices rush above about 400 tokens, and 600 characters is close to the 510 limit.

changes.change: Add the core player controls. playbackRate from 0.5x to 3x with preservesPitch, chips for 1/1.25/1.5/2, speed kept out of the cache key; ±15 s and paragraph previous/next; a sleep timer (15/30/45/60 minutes and end of chapter) checked in timeupdate, with a 10 s fade; tapping a sentence seeks to it; a 'Continue <title> at N%' card on the home screen; sentence highlighting through requestAnimationFrame. A rolling offline cache stores every fetched segment Blob in the Cache API by key and feeds MSE from it, and the service worker caches the app shell and library. A share_target with GET (title, text, url) imports links. Add a minimal first-run screen with the Samsung battery steps and an install prompt.
changes.reason: UX reviewer: speed, skip, sleep timer and resume are the most used ElevenReader controls, and without them the app feels like a prototype. The rolling cache costs little once segments are WebM Blobs, and it also covers Space outages, which is why the MeloTTS fallback can wait.

changes.change: Clone flow for Milestone B. Record with getUserMedia {echoCancellation:false, noiseSuppression:false, autoGainControl:false, channelCount:1}, as WAV through an AudioWorklet, with a level meter. Reject the take on a peak above -1 dBFS or a noise floor above -50 dBFS in a 2 s lead-in. The guided script is read line by line with per-line re-record. The script text is the transcript, so there is no Whisper. The Space converts to 24 kHz mono and keeps the best sentence-aligned 10-18 s neutral span, staying under the 20 s reference cap. Store {ref_key, ref_text, sha256}. Each preview is one GPU call of about 10 s and is labelled with the run it costs.
changes.reason: The UX, feasibility and audio reviewers agree that browser DSP damages the reference, that a 20-60 s reference does not match the 20 s cap, and that Whisper is redundant for a known script. Per-emotion excerpts (audio reviewer) wait for phase 2.

changes.change: Security baseline. Add `xtask bootstrap-token`, the only code that reads the Global API Key: it mints a 90-day 'nolabs-deploy' token (Workers Scripts, R2, D1 and Queues Edit; Tail Read). Without a scoped token, xtask refuses to run, and any mutating call on a resource without the nolabs- prefix panics before it is sent. Create a fine-grained HF token with read access to nolabs-engine only, store it as a Worker secret, and send it as x-hf-authorization; check once with the quota CLI that it debits the account pool. No R2 credentials in the Space: the Worker presigns SigV4 PUT/GET URLs (15 min) per object, with a bucket-scoped Object Read & Write token as the fallback. xtask generates the passphrase (128 bits) and stores its HMAC, with a D1 lockout after 20 failures per hour. The cookie becomes __Host-nolabs_s, SameSite=Strict, with a server-checked expiry and a session_epoch for revocation. No CORS middleware. Non-GET routes require Origin or Sec-Fetch-Site same-origin. Every HTML response gets the strict CSP from the security review plus nosniff. Ban inner_html, pin pdfjs-dist at 4.2.67 or later with isEvalSupported:false, and cap the EPUB uncompressed size. /api/audio accepts only [0-9a-f]{64}, and xtask asserts r2.dev access is disabled. Pin model revisions by commit sha, and put no secrets on argv.
changes.reason: The account holds 15 production Workers and pstream-data, so a Global-key bug or a Space dependency holding an admin R2 key would cause damage beyond this project. Imported HTML or PDF running JS on the session origin would have full API access. On SameSite: the UX reviewer asked for Lax so share-target launches work, and the security reviewer wins. The share navigation loads static assets, and the page's later same-origin /api fetches carry a Strict cookie.

changes.change: Space operations. Use preload_from_hub for Kokoro and its voices, en_core_web_sm and the Ming weights, all pinned by revision. One cron every 30 min reads GET /api/spaces/{repo}/runtime, calls restart when the stage is SLEEPING, PAUSED or RUNTIME_ERROR, records the stage in D1, and re-enqueues expired render leases. The consumer marks the Space unavailable when /health fails or no process_starts event arrives within 8 s, and requeues with backoff. Track a daily request counter in D1 and switch off background pre-render above 70k requests. Add an R2 lifecycle rule deleting audio/ after 60 days.
changes.reason: The feasibility reviewer showed that fallback detection and cold-start rebuilds were unspecified, and that the 100k requests, 10 GB R2 and 10k queue ops are shared with Streams.

changes.change: Text and voices. nolabs-text drops [digits] citations and superscript footnote refs, replaces other square brackets with parentheses, replaces URLs with their domain, joins hyphenated line ends, and skips code blocks and tables with a spoken notice. Curate Kokoro to af_heart (default), af_bella, af_nicole, bf_emma, am_michael, am_fenrir, am_puck, bm_george and bm_fable, with the rest under 'more'. Pre-render a 10 s preview per catalogue voice: Kokoro on CPU, plus the 4-5 English Ming voices in one GPU batch.
changes.reason: The UX and audio reviewers agree that a large catalogue of C/D-grade voices and read-out citations sound amateur. Removing brackets also stops stray [Sigh] in imported text from becoming a Ming tag.

changes.change: Code layout for testability. crates/core (pure: proto, text, cache_key, director validation, engine_error, budget, job state machine). crates/import (web only). crates/server (services over the Repo, Blob, Engine, Llm, JobQueue and Clock traits, with in-memory fakes and a rusqlite Repo running the real migrations). crates/worker (workers-rs adapters, router, SSE transport). crates/web (player state machine in Rust; interop/*.js as plain ES modules with JSDoc, no TypeScript). xtask (schema, deploy, smoke). space/nolabs_engine/{contract,engines/{kokoro,ming},audio,storage,errors}. Migrations are named NNNN_name.sql and tracked in a _migrations ledger with sha256, applied atomically per D1 batch. Tonight the web dist is embedded with include_bytes!, so the deploy is a single multipart upload.
changes.reason: The architecture reviewer is right that workers-rs types exist only on wasm32, so v1's 'unit tests in worker logic' have no seam. With no Node, TypeScript glue adds a build step that tsc cannot check. On assets, the feasibility reviewer's include_bytes! wins for tonight over the architecture reviewer's upload session, because the service worker caches the hashed shell and the extra Worker requests are few.

changes.change: Director, rebuilt. One entry per sentence: {sentence_idx, mode, emotion, confidence, tags:[{before_word_idx, anchor_word, tag}]}. Rust anchors and checks positions within ±3 words. Allowed tags: [Breathing] [Sigh] [Laughter] [Surprise-ah] [Surprise-oh] [Uhm] [Cough]. At most 1 tag per sentence and 2 per segment, and none in non-fiction. EMOTION mode only when confidence is at least 0.75 and the text is quoted dialogue. Emotion changes at most once per 3 sentences. On Standard, the director drives Kokoro multi-voice dialogue and ±8% speed and pause changes. Cap it at 6,000 neurons/day with a ledger. The director cache key is {model_id, prompt_version, schema, paragraph, context_hash}.
changes.reason: The UX reviewer is right that expressiveness should reach the default tier. The architecture reviewer is right that it should not ship tonight. The audio reviewer's anchoring and hysteresis fix the offset and emotion-swing failures that LLMs are known for.

changes.change: Ming quality. Load whisper-large-v3-turbo on cuda next to Ming and check WER inside the same @spaces.GPU call, re-rendering once with a new seed when WER is above 8% or the tail is missing. This adds GPU seconds but no extra run, and gives Ming word timings. Add per-emotion reference excerpts (6-12 s each from the labelled guided script) and expressive IP voices bootstrapped through EMOTION. Pair each Kokoro voice with a Ming reference and switch engines only at paragraph boundaries. Measure Ming fp16 and fp32 RTF on a Kaggle T4 and check the account's phone verification, then build the bulk renderer with the unchanged contract v1 and a 'render this book in my voice tonight' button.
changes.reason: This restores the ASR check both chats adopted. On where it runs, the audio reviewer's in-call GPU check wins over the feasibility reviewer's CPU faster-whisper, because a retry inside the same call saves one of the 3 daily runs.

changes.change: Remaining features. MeloTTS fallback per window with a 'basic voice' badge, its own cache key, and level matched through audio.volume. Whole-document Download through the queue at low priority. share_target POST for files. Bookmarks. PDF header, footer and page-number removal. Pronunciation dictionary in the cache key. Word-level Kokoro highlighting (chunk offset bookkeeping plus a misaki-to-source alignment). Full battery-kill self-test. CI workflow (fmt, clippy native and wasm32, tests, schema diff, pytest). Workers Static Assets upload session. Disabling workers.dev and previews once the custom domain is live, plus a WAF rate rule on /api/login. Voice deletion by the audio/<voice_id>/ prefix.
changes.reason: These are useful but not needed to replace ElevenReader tonight. Each one plugs into the v2 contract and job model without changing the Worker.

synthesis.justification: v1 gets the large decisions right: Kokoro on the Space CPU as the default with zero quota cost, Ming on the GPU for expressive and cloned voices, an always-on Worker with D1 and R2, and content-addressed caching. The five reviewers scored it 4-5 because the parts that make it work are missing or wrong. The Standard render path runs synchronously and breaks with the screen off. The Ogg format blocks gapless MSE playback. The director-to-Ming contract is rejected by Ming's own task validation (confirmed in tts_tasks.py). The design includes several Worker CPU traps, non-idempotent GPU calls that waste one of 3 daily runs, a cache key that serves stale audio, per-segment loudness that undoes correction 3, account-wide credentials next to production resources, and no test on the phone. v2 fixes each of these with a mechanism, and it cuts tonight down to a listening loop that can be verified on the device. It does not reach 8 or higher because Kokoro's real-time factor on the Space, the real run limit and Samsung's background behaviour are still unmeasured, and the cloned voice stays limited to a few minutes a day until the Kaggle path exists.

remaining_risks.risk: One UI kills or throttles Chrome with the screen off, so a long listen stops even with MSE and Media Session in place.
remaining_risks.mitigation: Run the 20-minute screen-off check on the A12 as a Milestone A gate, after setting the battery exemptions. Keep 3+ minutes buffered and the rolling cache local. If it fails, build the native shell (Kotlin MediaSessionService playing the same R2 WebM keys) as the next task.

remaining_risks.risk: Kokoro on the shared 2 vCPU Space renders below about 1.5x realtime, so playback at 2x speed or faster outruns rendering.
remaining_risks.mitigation: Pre-render whole documents on import through the queue, and size prefetch from the measured RTF. If RTF is below 1.5x, add the GitHub Actions Kokoro renderer (public repo, 4 vCPU) writing to the same R2 keys under the same contract.

remaining_risks.risk: ZeroGPU limits are tighter than assumed: 3 runs, an undocumented maximum duration, or a run-limit change. The cloned voice then delivers only about 1-3 minutes of audio a day.
remaining_risks.mitigation: Keep the GPU ledger, the per-day cap and the deferred state. Fall back to a Kokoro stand-in voice and never stop playback. Show runs left in the UI. Treat the Kaggle T4 bulk path as the real cloned-voice route and check it first in phase 2.

remaining_risks.risk: Shared Cloudflare free limits (100k requests/day, 10 GB R2, 10k queue ops, 10k neurons) are used up by the reader and Streams together, taking both down.
remaining_risks.mitigation: Record baseline usage tonight from the GraphQL API. Count requests and neurons in D1, switch off background pre-render above 70k requests, delete audio/ after 60 days with a lifecycle rule, use backoff instead of fixed polling, and cache audio in the service worker.

remaining_risks.risk: The Space is a single point of failure: rebuilds wipe the disk, an outage or a blocked creation stops new renders, and a dependency or upstream weight change breaks the pinned stack.
remaining_risks.mitigation: Use preload_from_hub with pinned revisions, the locked requirements, the 30-minute runtime cron with auto-restart, and a /health contract-version check. The rolling offline cache and pre-rendered documents cover outages, and MeloTTS in phase 2 covers new text. The source of audio is a config value, so GitHub Actions or Kaggle can take over without Worker changes.
